consequence.purge_user_data: Lost for good, once a second administrator approves: the account, its profile and every record of its data. Nothing can restore it.
consequence.approve_hold: The held change takes effect once every approver it needs has approved — if you are the last, now.
consequence.reject_hold: Lost: this request. The change is not made, and whoever asked for it must ask again.
consequence.unknown: The console does not know this action. Read it carefully before you confirm.
consequence.discard_job: Lost: this failed job and what it was asked to do. It is not run again.
consequence.mark_executed: The request is closed as done. Nothing is run again.
consequence.reapprove_hold: The change runs again at once.
consequence.withdraw_hold: Lost: this request. It is closed and never runs; whoever asked for it must ask again.
consequence.update_config: The new value applies everywhere this setting is read, as soon as it takes effect.
consequence.dual_control_add: Once a second administrator approves this, every change to the setting waits for an independent approver.
consequence.dual_control_remove: Once a second administrator approves this, a change to the setting applies without an independent approver.
consequence.capability_mapping_remove: An agent acting for an account can no longer use this capability: a capability with no mapping is refused.
consequence.replay_job: The job runs again from its first attempt, for the same tenant, and does whatever it does again.
consequence.job_turn_on: The job runs on its schedule again, for every tenant it runs for.
consequence.job_turn_off: The job stops running on its schedule until it is turned on again. A safety duty turned off may need a second operator's approval first.
consequence.job_set_interval: The job runs on the new interval from its next run.
consequence.job_run_now: The job runs now for every tenant it runs for, as if its time had come. Its schedule is not moved.
consequence.job_run_now_deletes: Lost: the records this job is meant to remove, for good. It runs now for every tenant it runs for.
consequence.effect_took_effect: Lost: the chance to call it again — the mark cannot be changed. The workflow waiting on the call goes on as if the service had confirmed it.
consequence.effect_no_effect: Lost: the chance to mark it as done later — the mark cannot be changed. The workflow waiting on the call ends without it.
consequence.provision_tenant: A new tenant is created, with these addresses pointing to it. It has no administrator until one is made.
consequence.add_tenant_address: Requests to this address are served as this tenant's from now on.
consequence.remove_tenant_address: Requests to this address are no longer served as this tenant's; anyone who uses it reaches the platform's own pages instead.
consequence.suspend_tenant: Everyone in the tenant is locked out at once: no one can sign in or use it until it is resumed. Its data is kept.
consequence.resume_tenant: Everyone in the tenant can sign in and use it again.
consequence.restore_tenant: The deleted tenant becomes active again and its purge is cancelled; everyone in it can sign in again.
consequence.request_tenant_deletion: Nothing changes yet: another operator must approve the deletion. Once approved, everyone in the tenant is locked out, and after its grace period every row it owns is purged.
consequence.approve_tenant_deletion: The tenant is deleted now: everyone in it is locked out. After its grace period every row it owns is purged for good; until then it can still be restored.
consequence.reject_tenant_deletion: The deletion request is closed; the tenant stays as it is.
consequence.make_tenant_admin: The account with this address becomes an administrator of the tenant: it can manage the tenant's people and settings.
consequence.purge_due_tenants: Lost: every row the purged tenants own, for good. Every deleted tenant whose grace period has passed is purged now.
consequence.update_tenant_setting: The tenant's own value replaces the one it had, for everyone in the tenant. A safety setting may need a second approver first.
consequence.reset_tenant_setting: The tenant's own value is removed: it follows the platform default again.
consequence.suspend_all_agents: Every agent stops acting at once, and the changes to the trusted agents list waiting for approval are withdrawn. Reactivating an agent is a change a second administrator approves.
consequence.ask_attestation: Nothing changes yet: a second operator must approve the attestation. Approved, the step is closed on your word and theirs.
consequence.approve_attestation: Lost: the step's open state — it is closed for good on the two operators' word that the identity was erased, without proof from the service, and the purge runs again.
consequence.reject_attestation: The request is closed; the step stays open.
consequence.resolve_review: The decision is recorded with your notes and takes effect for the account at once: overturning restores its standing from before the decision; upholding keeps it.

account_status.known_features: Every feature that exists. A feature not in this list is refused to everyone. It must name every feature the app's routes check and every feature the capability map uses.
account_status.restricted_features: Features a restricted account cannot use.
account_status.suspended_features: Features a suspended account cannot use. An asterisk alone means every feature.

admin.dual_control_actions: Administrative actions held until a second administrator who holds the same permission approves them. Never an action whose effect is a config write (an agent's registration or scope, a capability mapping): the key it writes is held under its own rules instead.

budget.default_tokens_per_month: Default monthly token budget per agent per scope
budget.default_usd_per_month: Default monthly USD budget per agent per scope
budget.max_cost_per_day: The most, in US dollars, any one agent may spend in a day across the platform. Each agent keeps its own lower limit if it has one: lowering this tightens every agent's spending; it never raises an agent above its own limit.
budget.max_steps_per_trajectory: The most steps any one agent run may take. Each agent keeps its own lower limit if it has one.
budget.tenant_max_cost_per_day: The most, in US dollars, all of one tenant's agents may spend together in a day, checked after each agent's own limit. Operators set it for each tenant.

agent.capability_features: Which account features each capability needs: a list of capabilities, each with its features. An agent acting for an account may use a capability only when the account may use every one of its features; a capability not in the list is refused. Change it on the Capability map screen.

delegation.max_ttl_seconds: The longest, in seconds, any token an account hands to an agent may last. A token lasts the shortest of what was asked for, the agent's own longest token, and this.

trajectory.abandon_after_hours: Hours an open agent trajectory (running, paused, awaiting retry, indeterminate) may go without activity, with no open hold on it, before the agents.trajectory-retention job ends it as failed. Retention then counts from its last activity.
trajectory.max_steps: Maximum steps per trajectory before forced completion
trajectory.retention_days: Days to retain completed trajectories before archival

agent.trajectory_max_segments: The most parts one chain of agent runs (an app session, or a run that continues into a new part) may have; each part holds at most 1,000 steps and 16 MiB. Past it, the next action is refused. Raising it lets one session grow larger.
agent.trusted_agents: The agents allowed to act for people: each with who answers for it, the capabilities it may use, whether it is active, and its longest token. An agent not in the list, or not active, is refused. Change it on the Trusted agents screen.

workflow.abandon_after_days: Days a workflow's open run may go without activity, with nothing waiting for approval, before the agent-run retention job ends it as failed. A workflow is its person's to continue; other runs end after the number of hours their own setting gives.

ai.daily_paid_requests_per_actor: Requests that make paid AI calls (model, translation, speech, song ID) one user or guest may make in any 24 hours; one request may make several calls. At the limit the caller gets 429 until requests age out. The platform uses 200 whenever this row is missing or outside 1–10000.
ai.prompt_cache_enabled: Whether a request to the AI model may reuse the model provider's cache of the fixed start of its instructions. A request must ask for it too, and only that fixed start — which holds nothing of any tenant's — is ever cached.

session.guest_absolute_seconds: Seconds a guest's session lasts from its start; a guest's session has no idle limit. Default 24 hours.
session.staff_absolute_seconds: Seconds a staff member's session lasts from sign-in, however it is used. Default 12 hours.
session.staff_idle_seconds: Seconds a staff member's session lasts without a request before it ends. Default 30 minutes.
session.user_absolute_seconds: Seconds a signed-in user's session lasts from sign-in, however it is used. Default 30 days.
session.user_idle_seconds: Seconds a signed-in user's session lasts without a request before it ends. Default 7 days.

auth.staff_mfa_required: Staff (anyone using an administrative permission) must sign in with a second factor. Turning it off needs a second operator.
auth.token_cache_seconds: Seconds a verified access token is answered from the shared cache instead of asking the identity provider again (at most 60, never past the token's expiry; 0: always ask). Sign-out, account, role and two-step verification changes void it at once.
auth.token_stale_grace_seconds: When the identity provider cannot answer (throttled, down), seconds past its fresh window an ordinary route may still accept a token it verified (never past the token's expiry or a revocation). Privileged routes never do: they answer 503. 0 turns it off.

config.approval_expiry_days: Pending approval requests expire after this many days.
config.dual_control_keys: Settings whose changes wait for a second administrator's approval before they apply, besides the safety settings under two-person approval. Change it on the Dual control screen.
config.require_two_person_approval: When on, a change to a safety setting waits for a super admin's approval before it takes effect.

coppa.blocked_features: Features blocked for under-13 users without parental consent. JSON array of feature identifiers.
coppa.consent_expiry_days: Days a child's account may wait for a parent's consent (pending or denied) after its age is recorded; then the gdpr.retention-purge job erases it (COPPA 312.5(c)(1)).
coppa.consent_expiry_enabled: Whether the retention job erases a child's account when the parent's consent is still pending, or was refused, past the days the consent setting allows. Off until parents can give consent in the app.
coppa.enforcement_enabled: Master switch for COPPA enforcement. When false, consent gate is bypassed (for development only).

effects.pending_timeout_minutes: Minutes an external call may stay pending before it is settled as of unknown outcome, for an operator to mark on the Jobs page.

guest.translate_allowance: Translate requests a guest may make before signing in (one per request, whatever the number of target languages). Enforced before any paid call; at the limit the guest is asked to sign in. The platform clamps it to 1–10 whatever this row says.

expire-restrictions.enabled: Steps restricted or suspended accounts whose end date has passed down to warned, for every active tenant.
expire-restrictions.interval_minutes: Minutes between runs that lift lapsed restrictions and suspensions.

trajectory-retention.enabled: Ends agents' open runs that have been idle for the set number of hours with nothing waiting for approval, then deletes finished and failed runs once they are older than the days the retention setting keeps them — for every active tenant and every suspended one (keeping data no longer than needed does not pause).

expire-approvals.enabled: Required and cannot be turned off: it ends configuration approvals that waited too long, settles approvals whose outcome is being checked, and lists runs whose outcome is unknown for a person to decide. Only how often it runs may be changed.
expire-approvals.interval_minutes: Minutes between runs that expire stale configuration approvals.

retention.enabled: Applies the retention rules no other job applies, for every active tenant and every suspended one (keeping data no longer than needed does not pause).

retention-purge.enabled: Erases accounts whose GDPR retention period has passed (hard purge), for every active tenant and every suspended one (a legal obligation that does not pause).

prune.enabled: Deletes jobs that succeeded once they are older than the days the job retention setting keeps them. Failed jobs are kept until an operator runs them again or discards them.

escalation-reaper.enabled: Applies the chosen remedy to escalations past their deadline, for every active tenant. Off, escalations past their deadline stay held back without a decision.
escalation-reaper.interval_minutes: Minutes between escalation-SLA reaper runs. An item can stay over its SLA by up to this long.

expire-strikes.enabled: Marks strikes past their expiry as expired, for every active tenant.

release-claims.enabled: Returns review items whose claim timed out to the queue, for every active tenant.
release-claims.interval_minutes: Minutes between releases of timed-out review claims.

jobs.retention_days: Days a succeeded job is kept in the history before it is pruned.

analyst.enabled: Runs the analyst agent over each active tenant's groups (group health reports in its trajectories).

curator.enabled: Runs the curator agent over each active tenant's groups (activity digests in its trajectories).

purge-due.enabled: Erases the data of deleted tenants once their purge date has passed.

moderation.appeal_reason_min_length: Minimum number of characters required in an appeal reason. Range: 1-1000.
moderation.appeal_window_hours: Hours after a decision during which a user may file an appeal. Range: 1-720.
moderation.blocklist_only_surfaces: Retired in 052 (D-20): nothing reads it. Kept, with its change history, as the record of what it was; it is not listed and cannot be set.
moderation.classifier_effort: Default effort tier for LLM classifier. Options: low, standard, max.
moderation.escalation_remedial_action: What happens to an escalation left past its deadline: block it (the default, and the safe choice), or escalate it higher (queue it again and tell a senior moderator). Allowing it is never a choice.
moderation.escalation_sla_hours: The most hours an item may wait for review, open or claimed, before the remedy is applied. Kept between the shortest and longest allowed; when it cannot be read, the shortest is used, so nothing waits longer than it should.
moderation.escalation_sla_max_hours: The longest the review deadline may be set to, so a mistake cannot leave items waiting for ever.
moderation.escalation_sla_min_hours: The shortest the review deadline may be set to — and the deadline used when the setting cannot be read.
moderation.extraction_severity_reduction: Severity levels to reduce for extraction content. Range: 0-3.

level1.block_severity: Minimum severity to BLOCK for Level 1 (under 13). Options: low, medium, high, critical.
level1.escalate_below: Classifier confidence threshold for escalation (Level 1). Range: 0.0-1.0.
level1.warn_severity: Minimum severity to WARN for Level 1 (under 13).

level2.block_severity: Minimum severity to BLOCK for Level 2 (13-17).
level2.escalate_below: Classifier confidence threshold for escalation (Level 2). Range: 0.0-1.0.
level2.warn_severity: Minimum severity to WARN for Level 2 (13-17).

level3.block_severity: Minimum severity to BLOCK for Level 3 (18+).
level3.escalate_below: Classifier confidence threshold for escalation (Level 3). Range: 0.0-1.0.
level3.warn_severity: Minimum severity to WARN for Level 3 (18+).

moderation.restriction_duration_hours: Duration of content restriction (read-only mode) in hours.
moderation.review_claim_timeout_hours: Hours a claimed review item may sit before it auto-releases back to pending. Range: 1-168.
moderation.strike_expiry_critical_days: Days until a critical-severity strike expires. 0 = never expires.
moderation.strike_expiry_high_days: Days until a high-severity strike expires. 0 = never expires.
moderation.strike_expiry_low_days: Days until a low-severity strike expires. 0 = never expires.
moderation.strike_expiry_medium_days: Days until a medium-severity strike expires. 0 = never expires.
moderation.suspension_duration_days: Duration of account suspension in days.
moderation.transcription_severity_reduction: Severity levels to reduce for transcription content. Range: 0-3.
moderation.translation_severity_reduction: Severity levels to reduce for translation content. Range: 0-3.

profile.max_real_name_length: Maximum length for real names. Enforced before Guardian screening.

settings.rate_limit_rpm: Default API rate limit (requests per minute)

retention.agent_budgets_days: Days an agent's daily spending counters are kept after their day.
retention.ai_metrics_days: Days an AI call's measurements are kept before they are deleted.
retention.app_sessions_days: Days an app session is kept after it was last updated.
retention.auth_sessions_days: Days a sign-in session's record is kept after it was last used or ended. Never less than the longest idle lifetime (30 days).
retention.content_safety_audit_days: Days a content-safety decision is kept before it is deleted; one that a strike names is kept with the account.
retention.effect_ledger_days: Days a finished outside effect (confirmed or failed) is kept in the record of effects; one still pending or unknown stays until it is settled.
retention.guest_usage_days: Days a guest's usage count is kept after the guest was last seen.
retention.network_identifiers_days: Days an IP address and a browser's description are kept on audit and consent records; the records themselves are kept, and only these two details are cleared.
retention.rate_limit_events_days: Days a counted request (a rate-limit event, which can name a network address) is kept, in every tenant, whether or not its counter is used again.
retention.user_interactions_days: Days a user interaction (an input, its output, a rating) is kept before it is deleted.

assistant.title: Assistant
assistant.intro: Ask a question and read the answer as it is written. Questions and answers are screened, as everything here is.
assistant.guest: The assistant is for accounts: a guest session cannot use it. Sign in or create an account to ask it a question.
assistant.question_hint: {count, number} of {max, number} characters. Ctrl+Enter (⌘+Enter on a Mac) asks.
assistant.stopped: You stopped the answer: what is shown is not complete.

account.title: Your account
account.guest: A guest session has no account, so no decision is recorded against it. Sign in to see the decisions about your content.

sessions.title: Signed-in devices
sessions.explainer: If you signed in on a device you no longer use, or think someone else is in your account, sign out everywhere. Every device is signed out at once, this one too, and each signs in again.
sessions.confirm_question: Sign out of every device, including this one?
sessions.failed: We could not sign you out everywhere. You are still signed in here. Check your connection and try again.

decisions.title: Decisions about your content
decisions.explainer: When our screening blocks something you submitted, it is listed here. You can ask a moderator to review a decision within {hours, plural, one {# hour} other {# hours}} of it.
decisions.none: No decision has blocked your content.
decisions.unreadable: Your decisions could not be read. Please try again.
decisions.unreachable: Could not reach the server. Please check your connection.
decisions.window_closed: The time to appeal this decision has passed.
decisions.appeal_sent: Your appeal was sent. A moderator will review it; where it stands is shown here.
decisions.appeal_waiting: Appeal sent {date}. Waiting for a moderator.
decisions.appeal_in_review: Appeal sent {date}. A moderator is reviewing it.
decisions.outcome_overturn: Appeal decided {date}: the decision was overturned.
decisions.outcome_modify: Appeal decided {date}: the decision was changed.
